findings.title: Embed template has a Ruby syntax error and cannot render
findings.body: best.html.erb closes its first conditional with `<%- end if %>` (line 6). That compiles to `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error, so ActionView raises when an existing embed topic is rendered and the iframe gets a 500. The new controller spec never renders views, so it still passes. On-demand and feed-imported embeds cannot display comments until this is a plain `end`.

findings.title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: Post#cook returns the raw body unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import saves remote HTML with that cook method (skip_validations: true). PollFeed (poll_feed.rb:35) runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the feed body first, which turns escaped tags back into real markup, and never runs Sanitize. import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes and still allows javascript: href/src values. TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13). Cooked HTML is treated as trusted in the forum UI, and best.html.erb:19 emits it with `raw`. A feed item or imported page can therefore store script or javascript: links that execute in the Discourse origin for every viewer of the topic or embed.

findings.title: Public embed endpoint triggers unbounded server-side fetches
findings.body: EmbedController#best is an unauthenticated GET. Its only gate is that the Referer host equals embeddable_host (embed_controller.rb:26), which any non-browser client can spoof. It then enqueues RetrieveTopic for the caller-supplied embed_url (embed_controller.rb:15). TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to that setting and does not restrict scheme or port (topic_retriever.rb:15). import_remote then calls open(url).read with no timeout or size cap. open-uri follows redirects, so a path on the configured host that 302s to a link-local or internal URL is fetched from the Discourse server, and the body is loaded entirely into memory. Distinct embed_urls each enqueue work, so this is also a job-queue and memory DoS, and a successful HTML response is imported as a topic posted by embed_by_username.

findings.title: Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin
findings.body: The embed layout calls parent.postMessage(message, request.referer). The second argument must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), but request.referer is a full URL with path and query. Browsers then throw or drop the message (target origin does not match the parent). ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`, so the string would not match even without a path. embed.js only grows the iframe from that discourse-resize message and sets scrolling=no, so comments stay clipped at the default iframe height.

findings.title: Loading embed never reliably advances to the topic
findings.body: When no TopicEmbed exists, EmbedController renders loading and then calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute (embed_controller.rb:19), marking that response cacheable. The loading page reloads itself after 30 seconds via location.reload() with no cache-busting flag, so the browser may reuse the fresh cached loading document and never notice that the topic was created. If the reload does hit the server, authorization still requires the Referer host to be embeddable_host. A reload's Referer is often the iframe's own Discourse URL or empty, not the original parent page, so ensure_embeddable returns InvalidAccess and the iframe stays on the error or loading state.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items
findings.body: poll_feed always calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS exposes standard RSS 2.0 bodies as description (and content:encoded as content_encoded), not content, so i.content is missing or nil and this raises NoMethodError. String#scrub itself only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so the same line crashes on Ruby 1.9/2.0 even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets retry: false, so one bad item aborts the rest of that hourly import. Titles and links are also used unchecked, so a blank title fails the same way.

findings.title: Feed URL is passed to Kernel#open with no scheme check
findings.body: poll_feed passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to open() after requiring open-uri. Nothing checks that the setting is an http or https URL. In Ruby, open('|...') spawns a shell and open('/path') reads a local file; open-uri only special-cases strings that look like URLs. A feed setting of a pipe command or filesystem path (admin UI, API, or script running as an admin) becomes command execution or local file read on the next poll. http URLs are also fetched with no timeout, redirect allowlist, or response size limit, so a slow or huge feed blocks a worker and can exhaust memory.

findings.title: Host-spam check still blocks imports for a new embed user
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, but PostCreator still runs rollback_if_host_spam_detected before save. has_host_spam? is skipped only for trust level basic and above, and newuser_spam_host_threshold defaults to 3. A newly created embed_by_username account is trust level 0, and imported HTML usually contains several links to the same host, so the create transaction is rolled back. import still treats the returned post object as present and TopicEmbed.create! then fails on a null post_id. Feed polling and on-demand retrieve both fail for ordinary articles unless the configured user is already TL1+.

findings.title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
findings.body: embed_url is a Rails string column, created as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Article and tracking URLs often exceed 255 characters. PostgreSQL then raises a string-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. There is no foreign key or dependent: :destroy on topic_id/post_id either, so deleting the topic leaves a topic_embeds row; topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead id, TopicView errors, and TopicRetriever skips the URL because the row exists, so the embed never heals.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten onto the article host
findings.body: absolutize_urls treats every href and src that starts with `/` as a root-relative path and strips leading slashes before prefixing the article origin. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/img.png start with `/`, so they become http://article-host/cdn.example.com/img.png. Relative links that do not start with `/` (img.png, ../img.png) are left untouched. Imported RSS and readability HTML commonly uses both forms, so images and links in the created topic are broken. The port logic also drops the port whenever it is 80 or 443, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 is rewritten to the wrong default port.

findings.title: Retrieve throttle can lock a URL forever
findings.body: retrieved_recently? claims the per-URL lock with SETNX and only then sets a 60 second TTL in a second command. If the process dies between those calls, retrieved:<url> is left with no expiry. Later retrieves treat the URL as recently fetched forever, unless the viewer is staff (no_throttle). The key is also set before a successful fetch, so a crash or a failed fetch in that window permanently prevents import of that embed URL. SET with NX and EX in one command would avoid the stuck key.

findings.title: Every embed miss synchronously imports the entire feed
findings.body: On a cache miss, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute inline before fetching the requested URL. That downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item, inside the RetrieveTopic worker that was enqueued just to import one page. One iframe view can occupy a Sidekiq thread for the full feed and create or revise every feed topic. The redis lock only lasts 60 seconds, so a slow poll overlaps the next retrieve and starts another full import. The scheduled job already polls hourly; this path should not repeat that work synchronously.

findings.title: Disqus import now requires live fetches and drops category and dates
findings.body: The importer used to create a local permalink topic with the XML thread's created_at and an optional --category. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote for t[:link] and the category option was removed, so every thread is fetched over HTTP, posted as the current time, and lands in the default category. import_remote is not rescued: one missing link, non-http link, timeout, or readability failure raises and aborts the rest of the export. The task can no longer import from the XML file alone.

findings.title: Embeddable host comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: invalid_host? and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compare SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI#host with != and do not downcase either side. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed_url of http://EvilTrout.com is rejected when the setting is eviltrout.com. The embed then 403s or never imports even though the host is the configured one.

findings.title: Poll feed specs do not exercise the guards they name
findings.body: The examples that claim execute requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. That setting defaults to false, so execute returns before those checks and the examples pass even if the url or username guard is deleted. Nothing calls poll_feed, so nil content, non-http item links, Kernel#open behavior, and TopicEmbed.import failures are untested. The embed controller spec also does not render views, which is why the best.html.erb syntax error is invisible to CI.
